title: Variable-root base enlargement makes a finite Tate fraction-field extension separable
statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $d\ge0$, $T=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_dangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], and $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$. Let $L/F$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $L$. There is a positive integer $q$, equal to $1$ in characteristic zero and to $p^e$ for some $e\ge0$ in characteristic $p>0$, with the following properties. Set $T_q=K\langle Y_1,\ldots,Y_dangle$ and let $\iota_q:T	o T_q$ send $\sum a_
u X^
u$ to $\sum a_
u Y^{q
u}$. This map is injective and $T_q$ is a free $T$-module with basis $\{Y^\alpha:0\le\alpha_j<q	ext{ for all }j\}$. There is an embedding $F_q=\operatorname{Frac}(T_q)\hookrightarrow\Omega$ extending $F\hookrightarrow L\hookrightarrow\Omega$ through $\iota_q$. For this embedding the compositum $LF_q\subseteq\Omega$, the smallest subfield containing $L$ and $F_q$, is a finite separable extension of $F_q$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. For $d=0$ the basis is $\{1\}$. No assertion that $F$ itself is perfect is made.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, purely inseparable variable-root enlargement in part (a), made precise for a general finite fraction-field extension before its Galois normal closure. Agent formulation: coefficientwise q-th roots identify Frac(T_q) with F^(1/q), and finitely many minimal polynomials have a uniform inseparability exponent. This strengthened preparation is not stated verbatim in the handout. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain, $K[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ is a domain; its restricted-series subring $T$, and likewise every $T_q$, is a domain, since the same zero-product implication holds in a subring and $1\ne0$. Choose a finite $F$-basis $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $L$. It also generates $L$ as a field, since its $F$-linear span is all of $L$. Each $a_i$ is algebraic: $1,a_i,\ldots,a_i^{r}$ are linearly dependent. Let $f_i\in F[Z]$ be its monic irreducible minimal polynomial, as specified in def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, part (a), variable-root enlargement; agent supplies the general finite-extension preparation and coefficient calculations (archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}K=0$, each $f_i$ has positive degree and nonzero derivative (its leading derivative coefficient is $\deg(f_i)\ne0$), hence is separable by lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative. Set $q=1$. If $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$, apply lem-trf-irreducible-separable-contraction over $F$ to obtain $m_i\ge0$ and separable $g_i$ with $f_i(Z)=g_i(Z^{p^{m_i}})$. Take $e=\max_i m_i$, with maximum $0$ for an empty family, and set $q=p^e$. The characteristic of $F$ agrees with that of $K$ because constants embed in $T$ and then in its fraction field. Thus every exponent $p^{m_i}$ divides $q$.

proof.text:
For any positive integer $q$, expansion $\iota_q$ is a ring map: the finite convolution formula for each coefficient respects the injective additive reindexing $
u\mapsto q
u$; the remaining coefficients are zero. Expansion preserves restrictedness and is injective, since the coefficient at $q
u$ recovers the original coefficient. For $b=\sum_
u b_
u Y^
u$, define $b_\alpha(X)=\sum_\mu b_{q\mu+\alpha}X^\mu$ for $0\le\alpha_j<q$. Each is restricted: coefficients above a fixed positive bound are a subset of those of $b$. Euclidean division of every exponent gives $b=\sum_\alpha Y^\alpha\iota_q(b_\alpha)$, uniquely by comparing the disjoint residue classes of exponents. This proves exactly the asserted free basis. For $d=0$ there is one empty multi-index and its monomial is $1$.

proof.text:
In characteristic zero $q=1$ gives the renaming isomorphism $T=T_q$, so use the given embedding $F\subset\Omega$ and proceed to step 7. Otherwise $q=p^e$. The coefficient map $	heta:T_q	o T$, $\sum b_
u Y^
u\mapsto\sum b_
u^qX^
u$, is a ring map by the finite convolution formula and Frobenius. Each $c\in K$ has a unique $q$-th root in $K$, since $K$ is algebraically closed and Frobenius is injective on a field. Moreover $|c^{1/q}|=|c|^{1/q}$, so taking these roots preserves restrictedness: $|c^{1/q}|\ge\epsilon$ iff $|c|\ge\epsilon^q$. Taking powers also preserves restrictedness by the reverse threshold calculation. Thus $	heta$ is a ring isomorphism. Iterating lem-weil-pbc-power-series-frobenius-coefficientwise $e$ times gives $b^q=\iota_q(	heta(b))$: the initial exponent is $1$ and each iteration multiplies every exponent and raises every coefficient by $p$. Extend $	heta$ to a field isomorphism $	heta:F_q	o F$ by $u/v\mapsto	heta(u)/	heta(v)$; this is well-defined by cross multiplication and preserves nonzero denominators. It satisfies $	heta(\iota_q(x))=x^q$ for every $x\in F$.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, part (a), variable-root enlargement; agent supplies the general finite-extension preparation and coefficient calculations (archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: In positive characteristic define $j(z)$, for $z\in F_q$, as the unique $q$-th root in $\Omega$ of $\theta(z)\in F$. Existence follows from algebraic closedness; uniqueness follows from $(u-v)^q=u^q-v^q$ in a field. The same identity and $(uv)^q=u^qv^q$ show $j(z+w)=j(z)+j(w)$, $j(zw)=j(z)j(w)$ and $j(1)=1$. It is injective since $j(z)=0$ implies $\theta(z)=0$. The preceding identity $\theta(\iota_q(x))=x^q$ gives $j(\iota_q(x))=x$, so it extends the required $F$-embedding. Put $E=j(F_q)$. Since $\theta$ is onto $F$, $E=\{u\in\Omega:u^q\in F\}$. In particular, for every $m\le e$, each $c\in F$ has its unique $p^m$-th root in $E$: take its $q$-th root and raise it to $p^{e-m}$.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, part (a), variable-root enlargement; agent supplies the general finite-extension preparation and coefficient calculations (archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: For each $i$ in positive characteristic put $q_i=p^{m_i}$. The unique-root map $\sigma_i:F\to E$, $c\mapsto c^{1/q_i}$, is an injective ring map, by the same sum and product identities. Apply it coefficientwise to $g_i$, obtaining $h_i\in E[Z]$. A Bezout identity $A g_i+B g_i'=1$ maps to $\sigma_i(A)h_i+\sigma_i(B)h_i'=1$, since coefficient maps commute with formal differentiation. Thus $h_i$ is separable. Also $h_i(a_i)^{q_i}=g_i(a_i^{q_i})=f_i(a_i)=0$, hence $h_i(a_i)=0$. The minimal polynomial $M_i$ over $E$ divides $h_i$, say $h_i=M_iR_i$. Its Bezout identity becomes $1=(\sigma_i(A)R_i+\sigma_i(B)R_i')M_i+(\sigma_i(B)R_i)M_i'$, proving $M_i$ separable. Here divisibility is precisely the kernel-generator property of the minimal polynomial. Consequently every $a_i$ is separable algebraic over $E$.

source.place: Tags 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), 09HC (fields-lemma-separable-elements); coefficient-root argument supplied by agent.

proof.text: In characteristic zero set $E=F$; step 2 already proves every $a_i$ separable over $E$. In either characteristic $LF_q$ means the compositum inside $\Omega$ for the embedding just constructed; it is $E(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, since $L=F(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ and $F\subset E$. Apply the final clause of lem-sfb-separable-generated-scalar-extension with both its base fields equal to $E$ and with $U=\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}$. It proves this generated field separable algebraic over $E$, hence over the identified $F_q$.

source.place: Tags 09H0 (fields-lemma-irreducible-polynomials), 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), 09HC (fields-lemma-separable-elements); coefficient-root argument supplied by agent.

proof.text: For finiteness, let $S$ be the $E$-linear span of the original $F$-basis $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ in $\Omega$. It contains $1$ and $L$, and is closed under multiplication: each $a_ia_j$ is an $F$-linear combination of the same basis and $F\subset E$. Thus $S$ is a domain containing $E$ and finite as an $E$-module. By lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree, $\operatorname{Frac}(S)/E$ is finite. Its fraction field equals $EL$: it is contained in $EL$, whereas any field containing $S$ contains both $E$ and $L$. Together with step 7 this proves the finite separable conclusion. If $d=0$, $T=K$ and the basis calculation in step 3 still gives $\{1\}$; no excluded-variable case or perfectness of $F$ was used.
